purpose: Three additional crane-perspective video drafts for user review; existing first clip retained.

params.prompt:
Animate the EXACT NINE cranes from the approved reference artwork as a coherent flock in continuous natural flight. Preserve the Japanese sumi-e black ink and neutral gray wash, ivory feather masses, dry-brush tapered tips and small red ink crown on EVERY head. Keep nine distinct birds with long forward-stretched necks, beaks, two naturally connected wings, and two long thin legs trailing backward. Each bird has its own starting wingbeat phase and subtly different cadence, with occasional individual glides; never synchronized flapping or identical repeated poses. Smooth physical shoulder/elbow/wrist motion and natural feather flex, no rubbery distortion, no stiff puppet or joint-rigged look. The largest near lower-left crane must retain natural smooth wing anatomy, without curled or hump-like shoulders. Camera tracks with the flock so all nine remain comfortably inside the frame at their reference relative sizes and distances; no cuts, zooms or camera orbit. Preserve the reference perspective throughout. A completely uniform bright chroma-green background fills the entire frame for later compositing, including between all wings, legs and feathers: no gradients, noise, scenery, ground, shadows, text, paint splashes, new objects or extra birds. No morphing, merging, lost birds, cloned wings, or birds exiting the frame. Silent clip.
Perspective 2: camera behind and to the RIGHT of the flock, viewing their backs and right flanks as they travel diagonally AWAY toward UPPER LEFT, with a gentle natural left bank. Keep this left-turn three-quarter view, and preserve individual wingbeat variety.
